name: Crest Whitestrips
summary: P&G's over-the-counter peroxide whitening strips; clinical trials show lightening of a shade or two, with sensitivity the usual trade-off.
lead: Crest Whitestrips are over-the-counter teeth-whitening strips made by Procter & Gamble under the Crest brand. Thin flexible plastic strips coated with a peroxide gel are pressed onto the front surfaces of the teeth for a set period each day over a course of one to three weeks. They were announced in 2000 and launched to consumers in 2001.

name: Custom bleaching trays
summary: Dentist-fitted trays that hold carbamide peroxide gel against the teeth; the long-standing at-home alternative to strips.
lead: Custom bleaching trays are thin, fitted mouthpieces made from a mould of a person's teeth, loaded with a carbamide or hydrogen peroxide gel and worn for a set period at home, usually under dentist supervision. Wikipedia credits an orthodontist with introducing tray bleaching in the late 1960s, and notes that a 1989 paper by Haywood and Heymann supported the method.

name: Whitening mouth rinse
summary: Peroxide mouthwash marketed for gradual stain lightening; the evidence base is mainly lab work and slow results are described.
lead: Whitening mouth rinses are over-the-counter mouthwashes containing a peroxide intended to lighten tooth colour or reduce stain. Wikipedia lists rinses among at-home whitening methods, describing use twice daily for one minute each time, with visible results that can take up to three months.

name: Potassium nitrate desensitising toothpaste
summary: Ordinary desensitising toothpaste that whitening users reach for to calm sensitivity; studied for dentine pain, not for bleaching specifically.
lead: Potassium nitrate desensitising toothpaste is a toothpaste containing potassium nitrate, a compound used to reduce dentine hypersensitivity, the sharp pain from exposed dentine in response to cold, heat or touch. In whitening communities it is mentioned as a product used around peroxide bleaching, because tooth sensitivity is the most common side effect of whitening.

name: Prophy paste polish
summary: The gritty paste dental hygienists polish with; used for surface stain, with research focused on materials rather than cosmetic results.
lead: Prophy paste is a gritty polishing paste applied with a rotating rubber cup, usually by a dental professional during a cleaning, to polish tooth surfaces and remove some surface deposits. It is relevant to appearance because it is used on extrinsic (surface) stain.

name: Lip suction pump
summary: A vacuum cup that temporarily swells the lips; no studies found.
lead: A lip suction pump is a hand-held vacuum device placed over the lips to make them look fuller. Wikipedia's lip plumper article describes such devices as using vacuum pumping to raise blood pressure in the lips, causing temporary swelling.

name: EarWell infant ear molding
summary: A splint system that molds a newborn's malleable ear cartilage into shape in the first weeks of life, with consistent but uncontrolled clinical evidence behind it.
lead: The EarWell Infant Ear Correction System is a non-surgical splinting system used to reshape congenital ear deformities in newborns, such as constricted (lop) ears, Stahl's ear and prominent ears. It is a molding approach in which a shaped device is adhered to the infant ear for a period of weeks .

name: Dermastamp 0.5mm
summary: A handheld needle stamp used for microneedling; forum users apply it to brows, skin and to push topicals in, while the controlled evidence is thin.
lead: A dermastamp is a handheld microneedling tool whose needle head is pressed straight down onto the skin, in contrast with a rolling dermaroller. A 0.5 mm needle length is a commonly discussed size in forum threads.
claims: Stamping reduces laugh and eye lines
Bimatoprost plus stamp reduces orbital fat

name: Red light mask (Omnilux/CurrentBody)
summary: Consumer LED face masks marketed for wrinkles and acne; the underlying red-light therapy has mixed, often preliminary evidence.
lead: A red light mask is a consumer LED device worn over the face that emits red light, sometimes combined with near-infrared or blue wavelengths, and is marketed for wrinkles, acne, puffiness and general skin appearance. Omnilux and CurrentBody are brand names associated with such masks.

name: Photorejuvenation LED panel
summary: Home red/near-infrared LED panel sold for skin rejuvenation; the mechanism is proposed and consumer-panel evidence is thin.
lead: A photorejuvenation LED panel is a flat array of light-emitting diodes, usually emitting red and near-infrared light, that users hold or mount near the face or body at home. Marketing and user discussion associate such panels with skin rejuvenation, including fine lines, texture and acne, and with hair growth.

name: Ultrasound scaler (home)
summary: Consumer version of the dental ultrasonic scaler for tartar removal; research covers professional devices, not home units.
lead: A home ultrasonic scaler is a consumer version of the vibrating instrument that dental professionals use to remove calculus (tartar), plaque and stain from teeth. Users in appearance communities discuss it as a way to remove tartar at home.

name: 1-Testosterone (1-Test / dihydroboldenone)
summary: A DHT-derived designer steroid once sold online as a supplement; controlled in the US since 2005 and untested in human trials.
lead: 1-Testosterone (1-Test, 1-T, dihydroboldenone) is a synthetic anabolic-androgenic steroid, the 5-alpha-reduced derivative of boldenone, differing from testosterone by a double bond at the 1(2) position. It has been sold as a supplement or prohormone for muscle building.

name: Methyl-1-testosterone (M1T)
summary: An oral designer androgen once sold as a prohormone supplement; known from animal work and a kidney-injury case report.
lead: Methyl-1-testosterone (M1T, SC-11195) is a synthetic, orally active anabolic-androgenic steroid, the 17-alpha-methyl derivative of 1-testosterone. It was never marketed for medical use. It appeared in the early 2000s in over-the-counter supplements aimed at bodybuilders.

name: Methylstenbolone (M-Sten / Hybrid)
summary: An oral designer androgen sold as a supplement or research chemical; no trials, with a case report of cholestatic jaundice.
lead: Methylstenbolone (M-Sten, Methyl-Sten, Ultradrol) is a synthetic, orally active anabolic-androgenic steroid, the 17-alpha-methylated derivative of stenbolone. It was never introduced for medical use and has been sold online as a nutritional supplement.

name: Methyldienolone (Methyldienolone / M-Dien)
summary: An unmarketed oral 19-nor androgen; almost nothing published beyond detection chemistry.
lead: Methyldienolone (RU-3467) is a synthetic, orally active anabolic-androgenic steroid, a 17-alpha-methylated 19-nortestosterone derivative. It has not been marketed as a medicine. Published literature is sparse.

name: Dimethyltrienolone (Dimethyltren / RU-2420)
summary: An obscure, never-marketed trenbolone analog with reported animal potency far above methyltestosterone and no human data.
lead: Dimethyltrienolone, developmental code RU-2420 and also written 7α,17α-dimethyltrenbolone, is a synthetic, orally active anabolic-androgenic steroid (AAS). It is a 17α-alkylated derivative of the 19-nortestosterone family that includes nandrolone, trenbolone and metribolone .

name: Metribolone (R1881 / Methyltrienolone)
summary: A lab-standard androgen receptor ligand that was dropped as a drug for liver toxicity and shows up in doping cases.
lead: Metribolone, also called methyltrienolone and by the code R1881, is a synthetic, orally active anabolic-androgenic steroid (AAS) and the 17α-methyl derivative of trenbolone . It has never been approved for medical use.

name: Tetrahydrogestrinone (THG / The Clear)
summary: The 2003 "designer steroid" built to slip past doping tests; potent in lab work, never studied in people.
lead: Tetrahydrogestrinone (THG), nicknamed "The Clear", is a synthetic, orally active anabolic-androgenic steroid made by chemically modifying the gynecological drug gestrinone. It was never approved for medical use .

name: Desoxymethyltestosterone (DMT / Madol)
summary: A 1960s oral steroid revived in 2005 as a designer doping agent and supplement ingredient; animal data only.
lead: Desoxymethyltestosterone (DMT, also called Madol and sold under names such as Pheraplex) is a synthetic, orally active anabolic-androgenic steroid, a 17α-methyl derivative of dihydrotestosterone (DHT) that lacks the usual 3-keto group . It is unrelated to the hallucinogen dimethyltryptamine, which shares the abbreviation .

name: Prostanozol
summary: A designer prohormone steroid once sold in bodybuilding supplements; now a Schedule III substance with no clinical data.
lead: Prostanozol, also called demethylstanozolol tetrahydropyran ether, is a designer anabolic-androgenic steroid that acts as a prodrug of the 17α-demethylated analogue of stanozolol (Winstrol) . It is taken by mouth .

name: Methyldiazinol
summary: A 1965 lab-curiosity DHT steroid with a high reported animal muscle-to-androgen ratio and nothing else on record.
lead: Methyldiazinol (3,3-azo-17α-methyl-5α-dihydrotestosterone, or 3-azi-17α-methyl-DHT) is a synthetic, orally active androgen and anabolic steroid that was never marketed . It is a 17α-methyl derivative of dihydrotestosterone, specifically the 3-azi (diazirine) analogue of mestanolone .

name: Epistane (Epitiostanol-derivative, Havoc)
summary: An oral designer steroid once sold as a supplement; case reports link it to liver bile-flow problems and nobody has trialled it.
lead: Epistane, also called methylepitiostanol, 17alpha-methylepithiostanol, Havoc or Epi Plex, is a synthetic, orally active anabolic-androgenic steroid derived from epitiostanol, a compound once used in Japan for breast cancer. It was never marketed as a medicine, but it has been sold online as a bodybuilding supplement since about 2009.

name: Methoxydienone (Methoxy / 18-methyl)
summary: A nandrolone-family designer steroid from contraceptive research that surfaced in supplements; no human trials exist.
lead: Methoxydienone, also called methoxygonadiene, is a synthetic steroid of the 19-nortestosterone group, related to the progestin levonorgestrel. It was never marketed as a medicine but has been sold online as a 'designer steroid' supplement ingredient.

name: Bolandione
summary: A nandrolone prohormone from the supplement era; now controlled and best known for causing doping-test positives.
lead: Bolandione, also known as 19-norandrostenedione or estr-4-ene-3,17-dione, is a steroid that acts as a precursor of the anabolic steroid nandrolone. It was sold without prescription in the United States as a prohormone supplement until 2005.

name: 19-Nor-4-androstenedione (19-norandrostenedione)
summary: A nandrolone prohormone from the supplement era, now mostly a doping-control footnote.
lead: 19-Nor-4-androstenedione, also called 19-norandrostenedione or bolandione, is a steroid that is a precursor of nandrolone. It was sold over the counter in the US as a prohormone supplement until 2005.

name: Trendione
summary: A trenbolone metabolite sold as a prohormone; studied mostly in cattle-manure environmental research, not in people.
lead: Trendione (estra-4,9,11-triene-3,17-dione; code RU-2065; nicknamed 'Trenavar') is a metabolite of the anabolic steroid trenbolone and has been sold online as a prohormone-type supplement.

name: Dienedione
summary: A trenbolone-type prohormone sold as a supplement until it was scheduled in 2010; no human studies exist.
lead: Dienedione (estra-4,9-diene-3,17-dione) is a synthetic, orally active anabolic-androgenic steroid of the 19-nortestosterone group that was never medically used. It is thought to be a prohormone of dienolone and was sold as a bodybuilding supplement, often marketed as a trenbolone prohormone.

name: 4-Androstenediol (4-AD)
summary: A 2000s-era oral testosterone prohormone supplement; sold on big muscle claims, with little human evidence behind them.
lead: 4-Androstenediol (androst-4-ene-3β,17β-diol, often abbreviated 4-AD or 4-diol) is an androgen-related steroid that was sold in the early 2000s as an oral "prohormone" dietary supplement, marketed to raise testosterone and support muscle growth. It is a close chemical relative of testosterone and is described as converting to testosterone in the body at a low rate.

name: 1-Androsterone (1-Andro)
summary: A designer DHEA-type prohormone sold online for muscle; known from seizure and doping-detection papers, with no human trials.
lead: 1-Androsterone, also sold as 1-Andro or 1-DHEA, is a synthetic oral androgen sold online as a "dietary supplement" for muscle gain. Chemically it is 3β-hydroxy-5α-androst-1-en-17-one, a positional isomer of the hormone DHEA.

name: Adrenosterone (11-keto-androstenedione)
summary: An adrenal steroid sold as '11-OXO' for fat loss via cortisol blocking; the pitch rests on a proposed mechanism with no supplement trials.
lead: Adrenosterone, also called 11-ketoandrostenedione, 11-oxoandrostenedione or Reichstein's substance G, is a steroid made in the adrenal glands. Tadeus Reichstein first isolated it from the adrenal cortex in 1936. It has very weak androgenic activity on its own and is an intermediate and prohormone of 11-ketotestosterone.
